newsitem.title: USA: BOXING-LEWIS HEAVIER FOR HEAVYWEIGHT TITLE FIGHT AGAINST MCCALL.
newsitem.headline: BOXING-LEWIS HEAVIER FOR HEAVYWEIGHT TITLE FIGHT AGAINST MCCALL.

text.p: Lennox Lewis outweighed Oliver McCall by 14 pounds (6.3 kg) at Thursday's weigh-in for their World Boxing Council heavyweight title fight on Friday.
Lewis weighed 251 pounds (113.8 kg), 13 pounds (5.9 kg) more than he weighed when McCall stopped him in the second round in September 1994 to win the WBC title.
McCall weighed in at 237 pounds (107.5 kg). That was six pounds (2.7 kg) more than he weighed for their first fight.

In an effort to hype the bout, which does not seem to have captured the imagination of the public, the two fighters descended from the ceiling of the Las Vegas Hilton's main theatre standing on opposite ends of what looked like a window-washing platform.

The 6-foot-5 (1.95 meters) Lewis was five pounds (2.2 kg) heavier than he has ever been for a fight. There was not much visible fat on him, but he perhaps did not have as much definition to his muscles as he has had in the past.
McCall, 6-foot-2 (1.87 meters), also appeared to be in shape, although just how much stamina and strength he has left after his recent drug problems remains to be seen.

McCall, 31 as is Lewis, lost the WBC title to Frank Bruno in September 1995. Bruno in turn lost it to Mike Tyson last March. The WBC crown was not at stake when Evander Holyfield beat Tyson last November.
